guard: detached spawn omits defaultAgent when an explicit agent wins or no caller default exists, while preserving a non-empty caller default as a distinct field
completionMarker: a non-empty caller default remains distinct from the explicit agent field
why: The suite imports the exact request builder used by detached spawn and validates its in-memory output against the closed manager schema from immediately before defaultAgent was added.
Every mutation builds the CLI first and rebuilds after restore because the request builder imports workspace packages through their dist entrypoints.
The three mutations separately restore the irrelevant explicit-default property, restore the undefined own-property, and drop the caller-default path.

mutations.cell: explicit --agent must omit the irrelevant caller default
mutations.name: restore irrelevant caller default beside explicit flag
mutations.find: ...(values.agent !== undefined ? { agent: values.agent } : callerDefault !== undefined ? { defaultAgent: callerDefault } : {}),
mutations.replace: ...(values.agent !== undefined ? { agent: values.agent, defaultAgent: callerDefault } : callerDefault !== undefined ? { defaultAgent: callerDefault } : {}),
mutations.expectRed: explicit --agent must omit the irrelevant caller default

mutations.cell: an unset caller default must not create a defaultAgent own-property
mutations.name: restore undefined defaultAgent own-property
mutations.find: ...(values.agent !== undefined ? { agent: values.agent } : callerDefault !== undefined ? { defaultAgent: callerDefault } : {}),
mutations.expectRed: an unset caller default must not create a defaultAgent own-property

mutations.cell: a non-empty caller default must remain defaultAgent
mutations.name: drop the non-empty caller default path
mutations.find: ...(values.agent !== undefined ? { agent: values.agent } : callerDefault !== undefined ? { defaultAgent: callerDefault } : {}),
mutations.expectRed: a non-empty caller default must remain defaultAgent
